# recover_string_table fixtures

Real `javascript-obfuscator` output, one pair of files per release, all built from the same
`source.js` so "recovered" can be asserted three ways: the markers are back as literals, no
lookup of the form `x(0x…)` is left, and the output **runs and prints the line the sample prints**.

| File | Generated by | Expected result |
|---|---|---|
| `source.js` | nothing (not obfuscated) | exit 0, `no string table found` |
| `obfuscator-0.27.4-plain-table.js` | javascript-obfuscator 0.27.4 | **not** recovered (exit 1): webcrack 2.16 leaves this 2019 layout as it is |
| `obfuscator-2.19.1-plain-table.js` | 2.19.1 | recovered |
| `obfuscator-4.1.1-plain-table.js` | 4.1.1 | recovered |
| `obfuscator-4.1.1-rc4-hardened.js` | 4.1.1: rc4 strings, rotation, shuffle, control-flow flattening, dead code, self-defending, split strings | recovered (14 KB back to the size of the source) |
| `obfuscator-5.10.1-plain-table.js` | 5.10.1 | recovered |
| `obfuscator-5.10.1-rc4-hardened.js` | 5.10.1, same hardened config | recovered |
| `legacy-layout.synthetic.js` | hand-written | **not** recovered by webcrack (its pass stops halfway), recovered by `--builtin-only` |

`legacy-layout.synthetic.js` is the one file no obfuscator produced. It is the layout the tool's
`--builtin-only` pass was written against (rotation IIFE as the first statement, unprefixed `_0x`
names, one-line wrappers); it exists so that pass has a test. It is **not** evidence that any real
sample has that layout: none of the six files above has it, and until v1.8.5 the pass decoded
nothing on any of them.

## Regenerating

```
npx javascript-obfuscator@2.19.1 source.js --config obfuscator.config.plain-table.json   --output obfuscator-2.19.1-plain-table.js
npx javascript-obfuscator@4.1.1  source.js --config obfuscator.config.rc4-hardened.json --output obfuscator-4.1.1-rc4-hardened.js
```

0.27.4 rejects the option set of the newer releases, so it gets `obfuscator.config.plain-table.v0.json`.
Output is random (names, order, rotation), so a regenerated file differs byte for byte while
asserting the same things. If a regenerated file changes an expected result above, that is the
finding: update the table and the tool's header, not just this table.
